web.title: Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B - Hugging Face
web.description:
# Qwen3.8-27B
These artifacts are compatible with Hugging Face Transformers, vLLM, SGLang, TokenSpeed, etc.

In particular, **Qwen3.8-27B** will be available as a hosted version with more production features, e.g., 1M context length by default, official built-in tools. For more information, please refer to the [Qwen3.8-27B Overview](https://www.qwencloud.com/models/qwen3.8-27b). The service is coming soon. Stay tuned for updates.

## Model Overview
- Context Length: 262,144 natively and extensible up to 1,000,000 tokens.

## Best Practices
3. **Processing Ultra-Long Texts**: Qwen3.8-27B natively supports context lengths of up to 262,144 tokens. For long-horizon tasks where the total length (including both input and output) exceeds this limit, we recommend using RoPE scaling techniques to handle long texts effectively, e.g., YaRN. YaRN is currently supported by several inference frameworks, e.g., vLLM, SGLang, and TokenSpeed.
In general, there are two approaches to enabling YaRN for supported frameworks:
   - Passing command line arguments: For vLLM, you can use VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN=1 vllm serve ... --hf-overrides '{"text_config": {"rope_parameters": {"mrope_interleaved": true, "mrope_section": [11, 11, 10], "rope_type": "yarn", "rope_theta": 10000000, "partial_rotary_factor": 0.25, "factor": 4.0, "original_max_position_embeddings": 262144}}}' --max-model-len 1000000 For SGLang, you can use SGLANG_ALLOW_OVERWRITE_LONGER_CONTEXT_LEN=1 python -m sglang.launch_server ... --json-model-override-args '{"text_config": {"rope_parameters": {"mrope_interleaved": true, "mrope_section": [11, 11, 10], "rope_type": "yarn", "rope_theta": 10000000, "partial_rotary_factor": 0.25, "factor": 4.0, "original_max_position_embeddings": 262144}}}' --context-length 1000000 For TokenSpeed, you can use TOKENSPEED_ALLOW_OVERWRITE_LONGER_CONTEXT_LEN=1 tokenspeed serve ... --hf-overrides '{"text_config": {"rope_parameters": {"mrope_interleaved": true, "mrope_section": [11, 11, 10], "rope_type": "yarn", "rope_theta": 10000000, "partial_rotary_factor": 0.25, "factor": 4.0, "original_max_position_embeddings": 262144}}}' --max-model-len 1000000

```
Alternatively, override the default values via engine startup parameters. For implementation details, refer to: [vLLM](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/34330) / [SGLang](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/18467).
```

| 6 | + |
| 7 | +# Qwen3.8-27B |
| 8 | + |
| 9 | +> [!Note] |
| 11 | +> |
| 12 | +> These artifacts are compatible with Hugging Face Transformers, vLLM, SGLang, TokenSpeed, etc. |
| 13 | + |
| 14 | +> [!Tip] |
| 15 | +> For users seeking managed, scalable inference without infrastructure maintenance, the official Qwen API service is provided by [Qwen Cloud]([https://www.qwencloud.com](https://www.qwencloud.com)). |
| 16 | +> In particular, **Qwen3.8-27B** will be available as a hosted version with more production features, e.g., 1M context length by default, official built-in tools. For more information, please refer to the [Qwen3.8-27B Overview]([https://www.qwencloud.com/models/qwen3.8-27b](https://www.qwencloud.com/models/qwen3.8-27b)). The service is coming soon. Stay tuned for updates. |
| 17 | + |
| 18 | +Following the widespread community adoption of the Qwen3.5 and Qwen3.6 series, we are pleased to introduce Qwen3.8, the most capable generation in the Qwen open-model family to date. |
| 19 | + |
| 21 | + |
| 22 | +## Qwen3.8 Highlights |
| 23 | + |
| 24 | +Qwen3.8-27B features the following enhancements: |
| 25 | +- **Core Capabilities**: Comprehensive improvements across coding, professional work, research, and long-horizon agentic tasks. |
| 26 | +- **Agent Execution**: Stronger autonomous planning and better handling of environment feedback, leading to more reliable end-to-end task completion. |
| 27 | +- **Downstream Compatibility**: Broader support for popular harnesses and development tools, making it easier to integrate into your existing stack. |
| 28 | +- **Flexible Thinking Control**: Thinking mode is on by default and can be disabled per request; reasoning depth can be tuned with `reasoning_effort`, and reasoning context from historical messages is retained via `preserve_thinking`. |
| 29 | +- **Vision-Language Understanding**: Native support for image and video understanding, from STEM diagrams and documents to hour-scale videos. |
| 30 | + |
| 31 | + |
| 32 | +## Model Overview |
| 33 | + |
| 34 | +- Type: Causal Language Model with Vision Encoder |
| 35 | +- Training Stage: Pre-training & Post-training |
| 36 | +- Language Model |
| 37 | + - Number of Parameters: 27B |
| 38 | + - Hidden Dimension: 5120 |
| 39 | + - Token Embedding: 248,320 (Padded) |
| 40 | + - Number of Layers: 64 |
| 41 | + - Hidden Layout: 16 × (3 × (Gated DeltaNet → FFN) → 1 × (Gated Attention → FFN)) |
| 42 | + - Gated DeltaNet: |
| 43 | + - Number of Linear Attention Heads: 48 for V and 16 for QK |
| 44 | + - Head Dimension: 128 |
| 45 | + - Gated Attention: |
| 46 | + - Number of Attention Heads: 24 for Q and 4 for KV |
| 47 | + - Head Dimension: 256 |
| 48 | + - Rotary Position Embedding Dimension: 64 |
| 49 | + - Feed Forward Network: |
| 50 | + - Intermediate Dimension: 17,408 |
| 51 | + - LM Output: 248,320 (Padded) |
| 52 | + - MTP (Multi-Token Prediction): trained with multiple steps |
| 53 | +- Context Length: 262,144 natively and extensible up to 1,000,000 tokens. |
| 54 | + |
| 55 | +## Quickstart |
| 56 | + |
| 57 | +For streamlined integration, we recommend using Qwen3.8 via APIs. |
| 58 | + |
| 59 | +### Serving Qwen3.8 |
| 60 | + |
| 61 | +> [!Important] |
| 62 | +> Inference efficiency and throughput vary significantly across frameworks. |
| 63 | +> We recommend using the latest framework versions to ensure optimal performance and compatibility. |
| 64 | +> For production workloads or high-throughput scenarios, dedicated serving engines such as SGLang, vLLM, or TokenSpeed are recommended. |
| 65 | + |
| 66 | +Qwen3.8 can be deployed with popular inference frameworks, e.g.: |
| 67 | + |
| 68 | +- [SGLang]([https://www.sglang.io/](https://www.sglang.io/)): [Qwen3.8 Cookbook]([https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/Qwen/Qwen3.8](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/Qwen/Qwen3.8)) |
| 69 | +- [vLLM]([https://vllm.ai/](https://vllm.ai/)): [Qwen3.8 Recipe]([https://recipes.vllm.ai/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B](https://recipes.vllm.ai/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B)) |
| 71 | + |
| 72 | + |
| 73 | +### API Usage |
| 74 | + |
| 75 | +> [!Important] |
| 76 | +> Qwen3.8 models operate in thinking mode by default, generating thinking content signified by `<think>\n...</think>\n\n` before producing the final response. |
| 78 | + |
| 79 | + |
| 80 | +> [!Tip] |
| 82 | +> - Thinking Mode: `temperature=1.0`, `top_p=0.95`, `top_k=20`, `min_p=0.0`, `presence_penalty=0.0`, `repetition_penalty=1.0` |
| 83 | +> - Instruct (or non-thinking) mode: `temperature=0.7`, `top_p=0.80`, `top_k=20`, `min_p=0.0`, `presence_penalty=1.5`, `repetition_penalty=1.0` |
| 84 | +> |
| 85 | +> Please note that the support for sampling parameters varies according to inference frameworks. |
| 86 | + |
| 87 | + |
| 88 | +Qwen3.8 comes with official support for `reasoning_effort`, which can be used to adjust reasoning depth and control cost: |
| 90 | + - `medium`: balancing accuracy and speed |
| 91 | + - `low`: efficient reasoning optimizing for speed and cost |
| 92 | + |
| 93 | + |
| 95 | + |
| 96 | +> [!Tip] |
| 97 | +> In multi-turn agentic tasks, lower reasoning effort does not always reduce overall task completion time. Although it may produce faster per-turn responses, it can also lead to insufficient analysis, more failures, and repeated retries, which may increase total latency and token consumption. |
| 98 | + |
| 99 | + |
| 100 | +#### Chat Completions API |
| 101 | + |
| 103 | +Before starting, make sure the OpenAI Python SDK is installed and the API key and the API base URL are configured, e.g.: |
| 104 | +```shell |
| 105 | +pip install -U openai |
| 106 | + |
| 107 | +# Set the following accordingly |
| 108 | +export OPENAI_BASE_URL='your-base-url' |
| 109 | +export OPENAI_API_KEY='your-api-key' |
| 110 | +``` |
| 111 | + |
| 112 | +##### Text-Only Input |
| 113 | + |
| 114 | +```python |
| 115 | +from openai import OpenAI |
| 116 | +# Configured by environment variables |
| 117 | +client = OpenAI() |
| 118 | + |
| 120 | + |
| 121 | +completion = client.chat.completions.create( |
| 122 | + model="Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B", |
| 123 | + messages=messages, |
| 124 | + extra_body={ |
| 125 | + "chat_template_kwargs": { |
| 126 | + "enable_thinking": True, # on by default |
| 127 | + "preserve_thinking": True, # on by default |
| 128 | + }, |
| 129 | + }, |
| 130 | + reasoning_effort="xhigh", # xhigh by default; supported levels are xhigh, medium, and low |
| 131 | + stream=True, |
| 132 | + stream_options={"include_usage": True}, |
| 133 | +) |
| 134 | + |
| 135 | +reasoning_content = "" |
| 136 | +answer_content = "" |
| 137 | +is_answering = False |
| 138 | +print("\n" + "=" * 20 + "Reasoning" + "=" * 20 + "\n") |
| 139 | + |
| 140 | +for chunk in completion: |
| 141 | + if not chunk.choices: |
| 142 | + print("\nUsage:") |
| 143 | + print(chunk.usage) |
| 144 | + continue |
| 145 | + |
| 146 | + delta = chunk.choices[0].delta |
| 147 | + |
| 148 | + if hasattr(delta, "reasoning_content") and delta.reasoning_content is not None: |
| 149 | + if not is_answering: |
| 150 | + print(delta.reasoning_content, end="", flush=True) |
| 151 | + reasoning_content += delta.reasoning_content |
| 152 | + |
| 153 | + if hasattr(delta, "content") and delta.content: |
| 154 | + if not is_answering: |
| 155 | + print("\n" + "=" * 20 + "Answer" + "=" * 20 + "\n") |
| 156 | + is_answering = True |
| 157 | + print(delta.content, end="", flush=True) |
| 158 | + answer_content += delta.content |
| 159 | +``` |
| 160 | + |
| 161 | + |
| 162 | +##### Image Input |
| 163 | + |
| 164 | +```python |
| 165 | +from openai import OpenAI |
| 166 | +# Configured by environment variables |
| 167 | +client = OpenAI() |
| 168 | + |

| 177 | + } | \ |
| 178 | + }, | \ |
| 179 | + { | \ |
| 180 | + "type": "text", | \ |
| 181 | + "text": "The centres of the four illustrated circles are in the corners of the square. The two big circles touch each other and also the two little circles. With which factor do you have to multiply the radii of the little circles to obtain the radius of the big circles?\nChoices:\n(A) $\\frac{2}{9}$\n(B) $\\sqrt{5}$\n(C) $0.8 \\cdot \\pi$\n(D) 2.5\n(E) $1+\\sqrt{2}$" | \ |
| 182 | + } | \ |
| 183 | + ] | \ |
| 184 | + } | \ |
| 185 | +] |
| 186 | + |
| 188 | + model="Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B", |
| 189 | + messages=messages, |
| 190 | +) |
| 191 | +print("Chat response:", chat_response) |
| 192 | +``` |
| 193 | + |
| 194 | +##### Video Input |
| 195 | + |
| 196 | +```python |
| 197 | +from openai import OpenAI |
| 198 | +# Configured by environment variables |
| 199 | +client = OpenAI() |
| 200 | + |
| 201 | +messages = [ | \ |
| 202 | + { | \ |
| 203 | + "role": "user", | \ |
| 204 | + "content": [ | \ |
| 205 | + { | \ |
| 206 | + "type": "video_url", | \ |
| 207 | + "video_url": { | \ |
| 208 | + "url": "[https://qianwen-res.oss-accelerate.aliyuncs.com/Qwen3.5/demo/video/N1cdUjctpG8.mp4](https://qianwen-res.oss-accelerate.aliyuncs.com/Qwen3.5/demo/video/N1cdUjctpG8.mp4)" | \ |
| 209 | + } | \ |
| 210 | + }, | \ |
| 211 | + { | \ |
| 212 | + "type": "text", | \ |
| 213 | + "text": "How many porcelain jars were discovered in the niches located in the primary chamber of the tomb?" | \ |
| 214 | + } | \ |
| 215 | + ] | \ |
| 216 | + } | \ |
| 217 | +] |
| 218 | + |

| 221 | +# This feature is currently supported only in vLLM. |
| 222 | +# |
| 223 | +# By default, `fps=2` and `do_sample_frames=True`. |

| 235 | + |
| 236 | + |
| 237 | +##### Instruct (or Non-Thinking) Mode |
| 238 | + |
| 239 | +Qwen3.8-27B will think by default before responding. |
| 240 | +You can obtain a direct response from the model without thinking by configuring the API parameters. |
| 241 | +For example, |
| 242 | +```python |

| 244 | +# Configured by environment variables |
| 245 | +client = OpenAI() |
| 246 | + |

| 248 | + { | \ |

| 255 | + } | \ |
| 256 | + }, | \ |
| 257 | + { | \ |
| 258 | + "type": "text", | \ |
| 259 | + "text": "Where is this?" | \ |
| 260 | + } | \ |
| 261 | + ] | \ |
| 262 | + } | \ |
| 263 | +] |
| 264 | + |
| 266 | + model="Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B", |
| 267 | + messages=messages, |
| 268 | + temperature=0.7, |
| 269 | + top_p=0.8, |
| 270 | + presence_penalty=1.5, |
| 271 | + extra_body={ |
| 272 | + "top_k": 20, |
| 273 | + "chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": False}, |
| 274 | + }, |
| 275 | +) |
| 276 | +print("Chat response:", chat_response) |
| 277 | +``` |
| 278 | + |
| 279 | +> [!Note] |
| 281 | + |
| 282 | + |
| 283 | +##### Disable Preserved Thinking |
| 284 | + |
| 285 | + |
| 286 | +By default, Qwen3.8 retains thinking blocks from all historical messages, maintaining a complete reasoning trace across the conversation. This behavior, known as preserved thinking, ensures full context continuity and is especially beneficial for agent scenarios where decision consistency and reduced redundant reasoning are critical. It also improves KV cache utilization, optimizing inference efficiency in both thinking and non-thinking modes. |
| 287 | + |
| 288 | +If you prefer to retain only the thinking blocks from the latest user message, you can disable this behavior by setting `preserve_thinking` to `False`: |
| 289 | + |
| 290 | +```python |
| 291 | +from openai import OpenAI |
| 292 | + |
| 293 | +# Configured by environment variables |
| 294 | +client = OpenAI() |
| 295 | +messages = [...] |
| 297 | + model="Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B", |
| 298 | + messages=messages, |
| 299 | + extra_body={ |
| 300 | + "chat_template_kwargs": {"preserve_thinking": False}, |
| 301 | + }, |
| 302 | +) |
| 303 | +print("Chat response:", chat_response) |
| 304 | +``` |
| 305 | + |
| 306 | +> [!Note] |
| 307 | +> If you are using APIs from Qwen Cloud, in addition to changing `model`, please use `"preserve_thinking": False` directly instead of wrapping it in `chat_template_kwargs`. |
| 308 | + |
| 309 | + |
| 310 | +## Best Practices |
| 311 | + |
| 312 | +To achieve optimal performance, we recommend the following settings: |
| 313 | + |
| 314 | +1. **Sampling Parameters**: We suggest using the following sets of sampling parameters: |
| 315 | + |
| 316 | + - Thinking Mode: `temperature=1.0`, `top_p=0.95`, `top_k=20`, `min_p=0.0`, `presence_penalty=0.0`, `repetition_penalty=1.0` |
| 317 | + - Instruct (or non-thinking) mode: `temperature=0.7`, `top_p=0.80`, `top_k=20`, `min_p=0.0`, `presence_penalty=1.5`, `repetition_penalty=1.0` |
| 318 | + |
| 319 | + For supported frameworks, you can adjust the `presence_penalty` parameter between 0 and 2 to reduce endless repetition. However, using a higher value may occasionally result in language mixing and a slight decrease in model performance. |
| 320 | + |
| 321 | +2. **Adequate Output Length**: To optimize performance on agentic tasks, we recommend allocating sufficient output length to allow the model to generate detailed and comprehensive responses. For frameworks that support separate token limits for internal reasoning and final outputs, we suggest the following configuration within the 1M context length: |
| 322 | + |
| 323 | + - Reasoning Content: Set the maximum output length to 262,144 tokens. |
| 324 | + - Final Response: Set the maximum output length to 131,072 tokens. |
| 325 | + |
| 326 | + These settings provide the necessary capacity for complex reasoning while ensuring ample space for high-quality final deliverables. |
| 327 | + |
| 328 | +3. **Processing Ultra-Long Texts**: Qwen3.8-27B natively supports context lengths of up to 262,144 tokens. For long-horizon tasks where the total length (including both input and output) exceeds this limit, we recommend using RoPE scaling techniques to handle long texts effectively, e.g., YaRN. |
| 329 | + |
| 330 | + YaRN is currently supported by several inference frameworks, e.g., vLLM, SGLang, and TokenSpeed. |
| 331 | + In general, there are two approaches to enabling YaRN for supported frameworks: |
| 332 | + |
| 333 | + - Modifying the model configuration file: |
| 334 | + |
| 336 | + ```json |
| 337 | + { |
| 338 | + "mrope_interleaved": true, |
| 339 | + "mrope_section": [ | \ |
| 340 | + 11, | \ |
| 341 | + 11, | \ |
| 342 | + 10 | \ |
| 343 | + ], |
| 344 | + "rope_type": "yarn", |
| 345 | + "rope_theta": 10000000, |
| 346 | + "partial_rotary_factor": 0.25, |
| 347 | + "factor": 4.0, |
| 348 | + "original_max_position_embeddings": 262144, |
| 349 | + } |
| 350 | + ``` |
| 351 | + |
| 352 | + - Passing command line arguments: |
| 353 | + |
| 354 | + For vLLM, you can use |
| 355 | + ```shell |
| 356 | + VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN=1 vllm serve ... --hf-overrides '{"text_config": {"rope_parameters": {"mrope_interleaved": true, "mrope_section": [11, 11, 10], "rope_type": "yarn", "rope_theta": 10000000, "partial_rotary_factor": 0.25, "factor": 4.0, "original_max_position_embeddings": 262144}}}' --max-model-len 1000000 |
| 357 | + ``` |
| 358 | + |
| 359 | + For SGLang, you can use |
| 360 | + ```shell |
| 361 | + SGLANG_ALLOW_OVERWRITE_LONGER_CONTEXT_LEN=1 python -m sglang.launch_server ... --json-model-override-args '{"text_config": {"rope_parameters": {"mrope_interleaved": true, "mrope_section": [11, 11, 10], "rope_type": "yarn", "rope_theta": 10000000, "partial_rotary_factor": 0.25, "factor": 4.0, "original_max_position_embeddings": 262144}}}' --context-length 1000000 |
| 362 | + ``` |
| 363 | + |
| 364 | + For TokenSpeed, you can use |
| 365 | + ```shell |
| 366 | + TOKENSPEED_ALLOW_OVERWRITE_LONGER_CONTEXT_LEN=1 tokenspeed serve ... --hf-overrides '{"text_config": {"rope_parameters": {"mrope_interleaved": true, "mrope_section": [11, 11, 10], "rope_type": "yarn", "rope_theta": 10000000, "partial_rotary_factor": 0.25, "factor": 4.0, "original_max_position_embeddings": 262144}}}' --max-model-len 1000000 |
| 367 | + ``` |
| 368 | + |
| 369 | + > [!NOTE] |
| 371 | + > We advise modifying the `rope_parameters` configuration only when processing long contexts is required. |
| 372 | + > It is also recommended to modify the `factor` as needed. For example, if the typical context length for your application is 524,288 tokens, it would be better to set `factor` as 2.0. |
| 373 | + |
| 374 | + |
| 376 | + ```json |
| 377 | + {"longest_edge": 469762048, "shortest_edge": 4096} |
| 378 | + ``` |
| 379 | + |
| 380 | + Alternatively, override the default values via engine startup parameters. For implementation details, refer to: [vLLM]([https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/34330](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/34330)) / [SGLang]([https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/18467](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/18467)). |

web.description:
## Benchmarked Qwen3.8-27B vs Nemotron 3.5 Lightning and Muse Glimmer on 16 hard problems (RTX 5090, Q4_K_M)
### Setup
- Ollama 0.32.12, tag `qwen3.8:latest` (Q4_K_M GGUF, 27.3B)
- 64K context, temperature 0.2, generation cap 32,768 tokens
- Every model loaded alone on the GPU, with all others unloaded and `/api/ps` polled empty first, so no run shared VRAM

### Where it struggled
[YoRandom](https://huggingface.co/YoRandom)

Also, I noticed your token speed for Glimmer running on vLLM it hits 190/200 tk/s on our 5090, which significantly changes the interpretation of your results, especially since in a concurrency setting it reaches up to 3100 tk/s, something Qwen absolutely cannot achieve with "only" 1600 tk/s.

On wsl with vllm it hit round 190+tps for me too.

Also, I noticed your token speed for Glimmer running on vLLM it hits 190/200 tk/s on our 5090, which significantly changes the interpretation of your results, especially since in a concurrency setting it reaches up to 3100 tk/s, something Qwen absolutely cannot achieve with "only" 1600 tk/s.

### On throughput, you are right, and my numbers do not contradict yours
That is a local workstation number, not a serving number. Your 190 to 200 tok/s for Glimmer on vLLM is a runtime and quantization difference rather than a model difference, and I would expect vLLM to beat Ollama by a wide margin.

### On thinking levels, that is a real gap in my run
[YoRandom](https://huggingface.co/YoRandom)

- We use a 131K context.
- vLLM NVFP4 optimized for a 5090.

[YoRandom](https://huggingface.co/YoRandom)

[YoRandom](https://huggingface.co/YoRandom)

One datapoint we can add from the same card, with a dtype his sweep does not cover: we evaluated this model under vLLM with NVFP4 weights and fp8_e4m3 KV cache, no MTP, temperature 0, 65K max context. 238 finance reasoning problems with one exact answer each, two full passes: 84.45% both times, identical.
